title:
Space engineering
Ranging and Doppler tracking
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS E-ST-50-02C Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue (31 July 2008), following ECSS-E-50-02A (first issue, 24 November 2005); ECSS-E-50-02B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The document does not state that it is superseded, and no later issue is in the library.

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Frequency assignment, modulation and spectral sharing
Compatibility with other ground stations networks (informative)

key_points.text: Scope: spacecraft ranged or Doppler-tracked over direct links to Earth stations (not via data relay satellites) in the Space Operation, Space Research and Earth Exploration Satellite services, with unprocessed ranging accuracies of 2,5 ns to 30 ns and Doppler accuracies of 0,1 mm/s to 1 mm/s.
Category A spacecraft are less than 2 × 10^6 km above the Earth's surface; category B are at or beyond that altitude.

The transponder is assumed to carry telecommand and telemetry on the same RF carriers as ranging; the system has five functions: Earth-to-Space link, transponder, Space-to-Earth link, link control and data acquisition.

Ranging modulation on both links shall be phase modulation (PM); the baseband ranging signal is a sine tone phase-modulated by codes Cn = Q1 ⊕ Q2 ⊕ ... ⊕ Qn, where Qi are square waves at 2^-i × ft, with code transitions at tone phase 90°.
Suppressed-carrier telemetry is not compatible with simultaneous ranging; orbit determination then uses time sharing between telemetry and ranging or a separate ranging transponder.

Code acquisition sequence: tone alone, then tone modulated with the sequence of codes, then tone with the final code; deep-space missions may restart the code sequence continuously for faster re-acquisition at reduced accuracy.

Earth-to-Space link: tone frequency selectable 100 kHz – 1,5 MHz, code period 2^n/ft with n = 0 to 20, tone modulation index 45° or 22,5°, group delay variation 20 ns/12 h pp (category A) or 2 ns/12 h pp (category B).

For deep space and two-way Doppler the transponder shall be coherent (downlink carrier derived from the uplink carrier by the turn-around ratio); coherent/non-coherent and ranging on/off shall be selectable by telecommand.
With on-board digital synthesis, the deviation from the ideal turn-around ratio shall not cause a Doppler bias above 0,1 mm/s averaged over 1 s.

For ambiguity resolution the ranging channel group delay shall be constant within ± 1/(5 ft) over 0,3 ft to 1,7 ft; for the measurement itself, constant within ± 30 ns at the tone frequency, as seen from the diplexer interface.
Typical on-board delay calibration accuracies are ± 5 ns for category A and ± 2,5 ns for category B missions.

Ranging measurement quantization shall be at most 1/65536 of the tone period, and station ranging accuracy 1 ns or 1/1000 of the tone period, whichever is larger; Doppler quantization shall be below 1/1000 of the carrier period.
For tropospheric correction the station measures pressure (± 1 hPa), temperature (± 1 °C) and relative humidity (±1%); the antenna phase centre location shall be known better than 0,5 m.
Compatibility tests use at least engineering qualification models of spacecraft equipment, often in a portable compatibility test unit ('suitcase').

Integrated Doppler measures the continuous carrier phase rather than independent velocity samples, giving a high-resolution change in range up to an unknown constant; it can be two-way (coherent) or one-way (non-coherent).

notes: The extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in document IDs. Figures 4-1 (functional block diagram, p. 12, partly extracted as loose labels), 4-2 to 4-5 (ranging spectra) and 4-6 (Allan variance curves) are graphics; Annex C's equations (p. 42) are garbled in the text. Superscripts are flattened (for example '2 × 106 km', p. 9; 'code length = 212' for 2^12, p. 5). The introduction's last bullet is printed as a separate paragraph (p. 6). Clause 4.5.2 refers to turn-around ratios 'in Table 5-1 of' ECSS-E-ST-50-05 (p. 28). Telecommand and TM data link aspects are out of scope; the RF companion ECSS-E-ST-50-05C Rev. 2 is in the library as ecss-e-st-50-05c-rev24october2011, and a later issue of CCSDS 401.0-B as ccsds-401-0-401x0b32. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 44 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 43.
